It isn't easy either some levels seem almost impossible but you'll be hooked on a good tune and improving your score.

I bought VR set for this game.
No regrets.
Cheaper than a gym.
Much more joy and satisfaction than going to a gym...

Excellent modding community, if it wasn't for that, I would definitively be bored out of my mind after going through everything.
Great workout as well, bought it with intension to help rehabilitate my left arm and back, and results have only been positive!

Was very cool, then they took away our 3rd party add-on tool, then demanded $2/song, and I haven't played much after losing my entire song library. The base game is still worth checking out, but with additional songs costing more than retail ... you'll either spend more or quit playing.

I love this game for the concept and execution. I hate it for its ineptitude toward its players, there were 10 songs at launch, and where are we now? Still ten. If you get the expansion (A cheap money grab) Then you got a whopping ten more! Now if you get BeatSaver, a free mod for the game, you get a community founded database of songs and charts including avatars, new swords, and even differing colours. Now why the devs didnt hire them to create a database backed by the devs I have no idea, but its apparent they had no concerns for how much play you can actually get officially, and instead were only worried about making more money. I havent played the game since September but for the short month I played this game nearly every day and had a blast, but the direction they seem to be taking is less than ideal with their greed and neglect to the community. TL;DR I love the community and the functions of the game, the devs are greedy

It may be quite a high price for the amount of work that went into creating this, but this is easily my most played VR game, so i guess it's worth the price.
Mods bring a ton of additional fun to the game btw..

Learn to play harder difficulties before the easier ones. Also play a lot so your arms don't hurt every time. Make sure you aren't facing a glass cabinet when you play. The base game has seemingly endless content, so don't worry about DLC when you first start.
Awesome game! Really smooth and good song. Love the many different options of songs you can choose from. Definently worth buying.

One of the best VR games i've ever played. I bought it several years ago and was plesantly supprised to see that they keep adding content to the game

Freaking awesome. I love this game. This is absolutely the game that got us to invest in a VR headset system, and honestly it's totally worth it. It can be relaxing on easier modes, or an intense workout on harder modes. Lots of songs available as part of the game, and various packs of songs for purchase as well.

The game itself is incredible, but I can't help but wonder if the devs keep constantly updating it with basically nothing new just to ruin the modded experience on purpose. Seriously, even the menu revamp updates add nothing to the experience.

Beat Saber feels barebones as a base game, the included DLC tracks aren't remotely interesting to me and a lot of people, and I gave money to Beat Games because of the mods, which they constantly screw with. It is a recurring problem that feels incredibly annoying.

If you own a vr headset this game is a solid starting point. Its fun for starters, it comes off hard at first but once you find your groove this game holds endless hours of fun, entertainment and a solid work out without even trying. I have not played in years but I"m about to get back into the vr scene and i cant wait to live out the experiences this game has to offer. Im bummed my review is this late but it was so good to this day its a solid must play for vr experiences!

Edit - The devs sold the game to Facebook which has bought it and is going to be releasing exclusive songs and making player made maps against terms of service due to "intellectual property".

Sure, I get it. But if you're like me and don't listen to mainstream music and popular music you're basically SCREWED cuz that's all this game is going to have on it. Also they basically answered ambiguously when asked if they are going to turn Beat Saber into an occulus rift exclusive!! So if you own a Vive you may be unable to play future content on Beat Saber

Beat Saber is the best VR rhythm game ever made. It is so good I don't think it will ever be topped. In the game the beat cubes fly towards you and it is your job to slice them with your laser sword. The game includes a campaign mode which is basically just doing different songs with certain handicaps and restrictions such as "play the song without missing a note, ect.". The game uses paid DLC to expand your song library but there is a generous amount of songs that are included.

I think most hardcore beat saber players mod the game to download custom songs without having to pay but that is unofficial. If you have VR, then this is a must buy.

pros: this game is like 99% perfect, and that other 1% is solved by mods and custom songs

cons: the devs feel the need to update the game for the tiniest things at times, breaking mods for a few days, and then will go silent for weeks/months. generally annoying but doesn't detract from the overall quality of the game.

must buy for VR enthusiasts
amazing rhythm game, only complaint i really have is the abhorrent price of dlc, theres over 200 songs at £1.65 each, on top of the £25 you're paying for the base game, you're looking at over £400

I like this game, but found the music selection to be a bit sparse. For example, none of Scatman John's discography is available to play.

I thought the iconic "Scatman's World" would be an obvious choice to include in the game.

"Everybody Jam!", released in 1996 would've made for a groovy addition.

"Listen to the Scatman" is a personal favorite of mine, and it's exclusion from this game was very disappointing.

For a VR game though, this title is one I am proud to have in my collection. Once they inevitably add the incredible Scatman John, this game will be a 10/10.

Great game when modded as it expands the pool of maps you can play so you're not just repeating the same maps. I recommend buying the game to both support the devs and make the game much easier to mod. The mod manager most commonly used does not work when Beat Saber is pirated(from my knowledge). That said, the game is very fun nonetheless and provides one of the greatest VR experiences. However, I would recommend buying it on sale if you can. If you buy the game here's a guide on modding it that I personally used: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2087115113, or just lookup "Beat Saber Modding Guide (WORKING 2022)" if you don't trust random links.

Update to my review: You can add your own music, HOWEVER this is a third party website and absolutely nothing to do with the base game.

Every custom song you can find on there was made by the community- which is fair in a sense, the people who made the game won't be able to cover all the songs.

HOWEVER, the songs you HAVE to pay for here that are absolutely OVER PRICED- you can totally find for free.

This game is probably only alive due to the community and the ability to add your own songs, which makes people's creativity spark.

My negative review is mainly aimed towards the greediness of the company, stopping people from playing good songs (third party sites aside) is just beyond the word 'greedy'.

Cannot recommend this game enough. I have way more hours than this because I own it on my Quest. Playing songs that I know is probably my favorite experience I've ever had playing a video game. Plus THIS GAME IS EXERCISE! If you're on the fence, pick it up, and mod it to have songs that you recognize in it. Seriously, you won't regret it.
